findings.title: include_website_name missing trailing question mark
findings.body: The new inclusion guard is defined as `def include_website_name` (without `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializer looks for a predicate method named `include_#{attr}?` (with the `?`) to decide whether to include an attribute. Every other inclusion guard in this file uses the `?` suffix (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_suspended_till?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`). Without the `?` the framework will not recognize this as an inclusion check, so `website_name` will be serialized whenever it is non-nil even when `website` is blank, and the `website.present?` check becomes dead code. This also contradicts the intent expressed in the new spec which expects `website_name` to be absent when there is no website.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) parsed repeatedly in website_name
findings.body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to three times (once for `.host`, and up to twice more for `.path` in the branches that append the path). `website` is also re-invoked via the `def website` method each time, which makes another user_profile lookup. This should be parsed once into a local variable (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused, and `website` should be memoized, to avoid redundant parsing/property lookups on every user serialization.

findings.title: Path used in display drops query string and fragment
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).path` returns only the path component; the query string and fragment are discarded. For a URL like `http://example.com/users?section=profile#bio` the displayed name will be `example.com/users`, losing information the user entered. If only the host/path is desired, that is fine, but it should be a deliberate choice; if the full URL minus scheme/userinfo is the goal then `request_uri` minus the scheme/host (or the original string with scheme stripped) would preserve the query/fragment. There is also no handling for non-ASCII/percent-encoded paths or trailing slashes (e.g. `http://example.com/` displays as `example.com/`).
